To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ACTANE consortium has identified a region on chromosome 22 that may contain a prostate cancer susceptibility locus.
the ACTANE consortium has performed a genome‐wide analysis of prostate cancer families and identified two regions on chromosomes 5 and 16 that show suggestive linkage.

the ACTANE consortium has identified a region on chromosome 1p that may harbor a prostate cancer susceptibility locus, and that this region is not the same as the one previously identified by the Cancer Genetics Markers of Susceptibility (CGEMS) project.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of novel methods for the analysis of genetic data.
understanding how the genetic and environmental factors interact to cause prostate cancer, and to identify the genetic factors that contribute to prostate cancer susceptibility.
the study of the genetic basis of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no convincing evidence for linkage in prostate cancer, and that further studies are needed.
there are no confirmed genetic loci for prostate cancer susceptibility.
the ACTANE Consortium has failed to find a gene on the X chromosome that confers susceptibility to prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have not found any evidence of linkage for prostate cancer to any of the 13 chromosomal regions we have studied.
there is evidence of linkage in the 5p15 region and in the 17q24 region, but the evidence of linkage in 5p15 is not as strong as it was in the previous analysis.
we did not detect any linkage signal in the 23 families that we studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many genes that contribute to prostate cancer, and the more genes we can find, the better.

we have identified a new locus for prostate cancer susceptibility on chromosome 17q21.32, and that the risk conferred by the rs6465657 variant in this region is independent of other known genetic and clinical risk factors for prostate cancer.
we have shown that there is a genetic contribution to the development of aggressive prostate cancer.
